## functions to add

**v0.1.0-beta** **Public release**

1.  Alex to dos

    1.  Allow for different primers per sample

    **Bugs found in a static audit of `R/` and `src/`, 25 July 2026.**
    Line numbers refer to the tree at commit `738464c`. Everything below
    was found by reading the code, not by running the model, so each
    should be reproduced before it is fixed. Grouped by severity.

    **A. Inference-affecting bugs (wrong numbers, silently)**

    1.  **`data$info` is re-sorted but `data$OTU` is not.**
        `y <- OTU` at `R/runOccJSDM.R:476`, then `data_info` is
        re-ordered by `dplyr::arrange(Site, Sample, Primer)` at
        `R/runOccJSDM.R:553-558`. Every downstream quantity (`M`, `K`,
        `sumM`, `sumK`, the `idx_*` maps, `X_psi`, `X_theta`) is built
        from the *sorted* `data_info`, but `y` keeps the caller's row
        order, so any input not already sorted by Site/Sample/Primer
        silently attaches each row of reads to the wrong site/sample.
        Data from `simulateOccJSDMData()` arrives already sorted, which
        is why the vignettes never hit this. Fix: compute the
        permutation once (`ord <- order(Site, Sample, Primer)`) and
        apply it to `y`/`OTU` as well -- or refuse to sort and error if
        the input is unsorted.

    2.  **Collection covariates are grouped by `Sample` alone.**
        `process_covariates(data_info, collCovariates, "Sample", N, ...)`
        at `R/runOccJSDM.R:673` does `group_by(Sample) %>% summarise()`,
        giving one row per *distinct* `Sample` value, sorted by
        `Sample`. But `X_theta` is indexed by the `sumM[i] + m`
        (Site-then-Sample) ordering. If `Sample` ids are only unique
        within a site (e.g. each site numbered `1:M`), rows collapse and
        `X_theta` has fewer than `N` rows; if they are globally unique
        but not ordered consistently with `Site`, the rows are permuted
        against `theta`. Fix: group by `c("Site", "Sample")`, matching
        the `M_df` construction at `R/runOccJSDM.R:564-569`.

    3.  **`sample_pq_cpp()`'s catch-all `else` inflates the Stage 2 FP
        counts.** `src/functions.cpp:652-668`. The R reference version
        (`sample_pq()`, `R/mcmcfun.R:160-189`) counts the four cases
        independently, each gated on `primerIdx == l`. The C++ version's
        final `else` catches every replicate that fails the first three
        tests -- including all replicates belonging to *other* primers
        -- and adds them to `w0_primerl_cases_0`, the "w = 0, no false
        positive" count. With `P = 1` the four cases happen to be
        exhaustive, so it is accidentally correct; with `P > 1` the Beta
        posterior for `q` picks up roughly `(P-1) * N3` spurious
        pseudo-counts per primer and every Stage 2 false-positive rate
        is biased toward zero. Fix: count the four cases independently,
        as in the R version.

    4.  **WAIC running means divide by the raw iteration counter.**
        `update_waic_summary(logliks, list_waic, iter)` is called with
        `iter`, the loop counter *including burn-in*
        (`R/runOccJSDM.R:1181`, `:1186`, `:1193`), and uses it as the
        Welford sample count (`R/mcmcfun.R:570`, `:576`), while
        `compute_waic()` divides `M2` by `niter * nchain`. Three
        separate errors follow: the first stored draw is weighted
        `1/(nburn+1)` instead of `1/1`; with `nthin > 1` the counter
        advances `nthin` times faster than draws accumulate; and `iter`
        restarts at 1 for chain 2 while the accumulator carries over.
        The reported `WAIC` -- and so the model comparison in
        `vignettes/occJSDM.Rmd` -- is wrong. Fix: keep a separate
        counter incremented once per *stored* draw, running
        `1:(niter * nchain)` across all chains.

    5.  **`sampleBuniv()` drops the residual precision (operator
        precedence).** `src/jsdm.cpp:579`:
        `tX * X * (1 / sigma*sigma)` parses as `(1/sigma) * sigma`,
        i.e. exactly `1`, so the likelihood is weighted with precision 1
        rather than `1/sigma^2`; the mean term `tX * y` is not scaled
        either. `sampleBuniv()` is the sampler for the trait-response
        coefficients `G`/`C` (`sample_GC()`) and the unobserved traits
        `A` (`sample_A()`), so `sigma_b` currently has no effect on any
        of them. Fix: `1.0 / (sigma * sigma)`, applied consistently to
        both terms.

    6.  **Non-thread-safe RNG inside the OpenMP loops.**
        `src/Makevars` enables OpenMP, and both
        `samplePGvariables()` (`src/jsdm.cpp:398`) and
        `sample_betatheta_cpp_parallel()` (`src/functions.cpp:600`) are
        `#pragma omp parallel for`. The work they dispatch calls R's
        RNG: `randinvg()` uses `R::rnorm` and `mvrnormArmaQuick()` uses
        `arma::randn`, which RcppArmadillo routes to R's RNG. R's RNG
        state is global and not thread-safe, so wherever OpenMP is
        actually active -- Linux and Windows/Rtools, but *not* stock
        macOS clang, which is presumably why this has not shown up
        locally -- these loops race. The thread-safe path looks
        half-finished: `mvrnormArmaQuick_TS()` exists, but
        `sample_beta_nocov_cpp_TS()` (`src/functions.cpp:301-309`)
        calls the *non*-TS `sample_beta_cpp()`, so it is never reached.
        Note `samplePGvariables()` is the hottest kernel in the sampler,
        so this is worth fixing properly (thread-local RNG throughout)
        rather than by disabling OpenMP.

    7.  **`Bs <- list_params$B` in `update_jSDMcoef()`.**
        `R/jsdmfun.R:940` -- should be `list_params$Bs`. Consequence:
        `ps <- ncol(Bs)` at `R/jsdmfun.R:971` evaluates to `S` rather
        than the number of spatial support points, so every
        `if (ps > 0)` spatial branch runs unconditionally, even for
        models with no spatial field. The inner guards keep most of them
        no-ops, but `sigma_bs` is redrawn from its prior every iteration
        in non-spatial models.

    8.  **`sigma_bs` is sampled but never used.** `sample_BBsL()` takes
        `sigma_bs` as an argument and never references it; the spatial
        block of the prior covariance is left at `diag(1)`
        (`R/jsdmfun.R:711-713`, cf. the `sigma_b^2` line immediately
        above it). So the spatial coefficients' prior variance is
        hard-coded to 1, and `sigmabs_output` reports a posterior for a
        parameter that does not enter the model.

    9.  **The GP length-scale is never updated.** The `sample_ls()` call
        in `update_jSDMcoef()` is wrapped in `if(F){...}`
        (`R/jsdmfun.R:1063`), so `idx_ls` stays at its hard-coded
        starting value of 3 for the entire run -- `l_s` is fixed at
        `l_s_grid[3]` (about 0.074 on the standardised coordinate
        scale) and `idx_ls_output` is a constant. Either re-enable it
        (`sample_ls()` also needs fixing: it references a global `S`,
        and is called with `Bs` where the signature expects `SE`) or
        document that the spatial range is fixed and expose it as an
        argument.

    10. **`useBiotic` is ignored in `computeNewOutputs()`.**
        `src/jsdm.cpp:501` tests `useEnvCov` a second time where it
        should test `useBiotic`, so the latent-factor term is included
        exactly when the environmental term is.
        `predictNewSites(useEnvCov = FALSE, useBiotic = TRUE)` silently
        drops the factor term, and `useEnvCov = TRUE, useBiotic = FALSE`
        silently keeps it.

    11. **`simulateData()` adds the spatial field *after* the responses
        are drawn.** `R/jsdmfun.R:429-455` draw `z` from `eta`; only
        then, at `:457-461`, is `eta <- eta + spatField` applied. With
        `useSpatField = TRUE` the returned data therefore contain no
        spatial autocorrelation at all, while `trueParams$eta` and
        `trueParams$varPart` report as though they do. This makes the
        `useSpatField` sections of
        `vignettes/simulateOccJSDMData.Rmd` misleading and would defeat
        any test that tries to recover a simulated spatial signal.

    12. **`transformCovariatesMatrix()` never applies the stored factor
        levels.** `R/runOccJSDM.R:38` does
        `levels(df[,col]) <- cat_levels[[col]]`, but `df[,col]` on a
        tibble/data.frame is a one-column *data frame*, so `levels<-`
        attaches a stray attribute instead of re-levelling the column
        (it needs `df[[col]]`). Model fitting is unaffected (the column
        is already a factor), but re-levelling new data is the entire
        purpose of this code path: new data missing a level, or with
        levels in a different order, yields a design matrix whose
        columns do not match the fitted coefficients. Affects
        `predictNewSites()` and `createSpatialPredMatrix()`.

    13. **`listPriors$prior_beta_psi` / `prior_beta_psi_sd` have no
        effect.** Read at `R/runOccJSDM.R:738-739` and documented under
        `@param listPriors`, but the only consumers
        (`sample_betapsiLL()`, `sample_LL()`, `sample_betapsis()` in
        `R/mcmcfun.R`) are no longer called -- the live path is
        `update_jSDMcoef()` -> `sample_BBsL()`, which hard-codes the
        occupancy prior. Either wire them through or drop them from the
        docs. (Also, `ifelse()` is the wrong idiom for these scalar
        defaults: it silently truncates a vector-valued prior to its
        first element. `get_param()` is already available.)

    14. **`sigma_h` is never sampled.** Initialised to 1
        (`R/runOccJSDM.R:1009`) and passed through `update_jSDMcoef()`
        unchanged, so `sigmah_output` is constant.
        `predictNewSites()` uses it as the factor-score SD when
        simulating `U` at new sites (`src/jsdm.cpp:487`), so
        predictions silently assume unit factor variance.

    15. **`tau_output` is returned entirely `NA`.**
        `tau_output_chain` is allocated (`R/runOccJSDM.R:934`) and
        copied out (`:1236`), but never written inside the sampling
        loop -- the save block at `:1157-1176` stores every other JSDM
        parameter except `tau`.

    **B. Crashes, unreachable code paths, and API bugs**

    1.  **`summarisedLatentPresences = FALSE` errors on two-stage
        models.** The `w_output_mean` accumulation at
        `R/runOccJSDM.R:1152` is unconditional, but `w_output_mean` is
        only created in the `summarisedLatentPresences = TRUE` branch
        (`:861`), so the first stored iteration fails with
        `object 'w_output_mean' not found`. Relatedly,
        `w_output_chain` (`:913`) and `theta_output_chain` (`:905`) are
        allocated and never written, and `results_output$w_output` is
        set unconditionally from `w_output_mean` (`:1317`), so the full
        `w` samples would be discarded even once the crash is fixed.

    2.  **`thinOutput()` cannot run at all.** `R/output.R:21` reads
        `niter` from `results_output$beta_ord_output`, an array that no
        longer exists, so `seq(1, NULL, by = 5)` errors immediately. The
        `thin` argument is also ignored (`by = 5` is hard-coded), and
        the non-`z_output` branch thins any 2-D element *by row* --
        which would silently drop sites from the `psi_output` /
        `w_output` / `theta_output` posterior-mean matrices -- while
        the scalar `WAIC` falls through to
        `print("Dimension not recognised")` and becomes `NULL`. Worth
        fixing properly, since post-hoc thinning is the intended route
        to shrinking the 62 MB `data/sampleresults.rda`.

    3.  **`spatCovariates` is assumed to be exactly two columns, and
        never checked.** The GP kernel `k2_cpp()`
        (`src/jsdm.cpp:372-375`) and the support-point distance in
        `computeSpatialSummaries()` both read only the first two
        coordinates. Three or more spatial covariates are silently
        ignored past the second; a single one reads `x1[1]` off the end
        of the row (undefined behaviour -- Armadillo does not
        bounds-check in release builds). Add an explicit
        `length(spatCovariates) == 2` check in `runOccJSDM()`.

    4.  **`computeDiagnostics()` runs on `psi_output`.**
        `R/diagnostics.R:403-404` skips `z_output` / `w_output` /
        `theta_output` / `idx_ls_output` / `varPart_output`, but not
        `psi_output`. Under the default
        `summarisedLatentPresences = TRUE`, `psi_output` is an `n x S`
        matrix of posterior means, which
        `array(arr, dim = c(1, niter, nchain))` (`:422`) silently
        recycles or truncates into meaningless "psi" R-hat and ESS
        values printed at the end of every fit. Add `psi_output` to the
        skip list.

    5.  **`predictNewSites()` does not honour its documented no-op
        behaviour.** The docs say `useEnvCov` / `useSpatial` are
        "ignored ... if no [covariates / spatial field] were
        estimated", but `R/output.R:1457` and `:1470` branch on the flag
        alone. With the defaults (`TRUE`), a JSDM fit with no occupancy
        covariates calls `transformCovariatesMatrix(X_psi, NULL, ...)`,
        and a fit with no spatial field calls
        `createSpatialPredMatrix()` with an empty `X_tilde`. `X_psi` and
        `X_s` also lack defaults, so `predictNewSites(fit, X_psi = X)`
        fails on the missing `X_s` promise even when
        `useSpatial = FALSE`; give both `NULL` defaults.

    6.  **`returnLatentPresences()` is two-stage only.**
        `R/output.R:1709` and `:1715-1719` index
        `data_info[, c("Site","Sample","Primer")]` and
        `list_idx$idx_z_k` / `idx_w_k` / `idx_p_k`, all of which are
        absent or `NULL` for one-stage occupancy and JSDM-only fits.
        Either support those models or `stop()` with a clear message, as
        `plotDetectionRates()` and
        `plotCumulativeSpeciesDetections()` already do.

    7.  **`set.seed(1)` inside `computeSpeciesDetected()`.**
        `R/output.R:2222` resets the user's global RNG stream as a side
        effect of drawing a plot. Save and restore `.Random.seed`
        instead (or use `withr::with_seed()`).

    8.  **`computeSpeciesDetected()` uses the first 200 draws, not a
        posterior sample.** `R/output.R:2206-2207` flatten the chains
        and then index `b = 1:200`, which is iterations 1-200 of chain 1
        only -- the most autocorrelated draws in the run, ignoring chain
        2 entirely. It is also unguarded: fewer than 200 stored draws is
        a subscript error. Fix: draw `B` indices at random from
        `seq_len(niter * nchain)`.

    9.  **Species-ordering bug shared by four plotting functions.**
        `plotOccupancyRates()` (`R/output.R:513-516`),
        `plotCollectionRates()` (`:701`),
        `plotFPTPStage2Rates()` (`:789`) and
        `plotStage1FPRates()` (`:949-952`) each compute `order()` on the
        *filtered* `data_plot` and then use the result to index the
        *unfiltered* `speciesNames`. For any `idx_species` other than a
        prefix `1:k`, the factor levels name the wrong species and the
        bars silently disappear. `plotCollectionRates()` also accepts
        `idx_species` and never uses it -- the filter is commented out
        at `:698`.

    10. **`plotFPTPStage2Rates()` still ignores `primerName`.**
        `R/output.R:767` and `:775` use `apply(p_output, 2, ...)`, which
        pools over primer, iteration and chain, so the plot is identical
        whatever `primerName` is passed. The
        `idx_speciesprimer <- str_match(...)` line at `:784` is dead
        code. (Previously noted in `AGENTS.md`; recorded here so it is
        tracked as a to-do.)

    11. **Assorted smaller items.**
        (a) `createDataIdx()` is called with `maxP`
        (`R/runOccJSDM.R:638`) for `model = "occupancy"` too, where
        `maxP` was never assigned -- it survives only because R's lazy
        evaluation never forces the promise; pass `NULL` explicitly.
        (b) `c_imk <- as.numeric(y > 0)` (`:963`) drops the matrix
        dimensions, harmless only because `c_imk` is overwritten at
        `:1104` before first use.
        (c) `d <- get_param(listParams, "n_factors")` defaults to 0, and
        the cap at `:716` uses `ncol(OTU)`, which is `NULL` for a
        single-species vector `OTU` -- `if (d > NULL)` errors.
        (d) `reparamFactorModel(A_output, C_output)` (`:1273`) assumes
        `qr.Q()` is square; when `ncov_psi < gt` it is not, and
        `diag(diag(R_current), nrow = d)` recycles.
        (e) The spatial-covariate numeric check at `:540` runs *before*
        the "names present in `data$info`" check at `:544`, so a
        mistyped spatial covariate name gives
        `undefined columns selected` rather than the intended message.
        (f) `simulateOccJSDMData()`'s `@details` still says "For
        two-stage eDNA data specifically, use `simulateOccJSDMData()`"
        -- a self-reference left over from the merge of
        `simulateOccJSDMDataGeneral()`.
        (g) `computeSpeciesDetected()`'s roxygen still documents the
        removed Beta-approximation signature (`ab_p`, `K`, `primer`,
        `alpha`) instead of its actual arguments.

    **C. Dead and broken internal code**

    None of this is reachable from an exported function, but it will
    draw `R CMD check` "no visible binding" notes and is a trap for
    anyone reading the source. Suggest moving the genuinely dead
    functions to `deprecated/` and wiring up the two missing imports.

    1.  `R/mcmcfun.R`: `sample_z()`, `sample_w()` and `sample_cimk()`
        reference undeclared globals (`M`, `sumM`, `n`, `z`, `w`, `y`);
        `loglik_sigma1()` (`:547`) is an unfinished stub whose entire
        body is `p[primerIdx[]]`. All are superseded by the `_cpp`
        versions.

    2.  `R/jsdmfun.R`: `sample_BCsL()` references undefined `U` / `gt` /
        `gts`; `sample_U()`, `sample_Br()` and `sample_BL_fixed()`
        reference globals `S` / `U` / `n`; `computePredictiveProbs()`
        references `fitModel`, `psi_output`, `X_ord` and
        `beta_ord_output`, none of which exist; `partition_r2()` calls
        `pseudo_R2()` with one argument (it takes two);
        `returnSpatialEffectMean()` and `plotSpatialEffect()` reference
        a global `Xs_centers` and a nonexistent `returnSpatialEffect()`.

    3.  `R/output.R`: `plotReadIntensity()` reads
        `results_output$mu1_output` / `mu0_output` / `sigma1_output` /
        `sigma0_output` and `infos$maxexplogy1`, none of which
        `runOccJSDM()` produces any more; `plotOccupancyStates()`
        references undefined `data_info` / `OTU`.

    4.  **Missing imports for code that *is* live**:
        `plotCovariateTrend()` (`R/jsdmfun.R:1552`) calls
        `pivot_longer()` and `createSplinesObjects()` (`:245`) calls
        `ns()`, but neither `tidyr` nor `splines` is imported in
        `NAMESPACE`. (`createSplinesObjects()` also ignores its own
        `df` argument and hard-codes `df = 5`.)

    **D. Performance of `runOccJSDM()`**

    Ordered by expected speedup per unit of effort. Nothing here has
    been profiled -- worth running `profvis::profvis()` on a vignette-
    sized fit first to confirm where the time actually goes.

    1.  **Parallelise over chains -- but use a PSOCK cluster, not
        `mclapply()`.** The `for (chain in 1:nchain)` loop
        (`R/runOccJSDM.R:895`) is serial and embarrassingly parallel;
        each chain touches only its own `*_output_chain` arrays, so
        running the chains in separate *processes* gives close to an
        `nchain`-fold speedup and sidesteps the RNG thread-safety
        problem in bug A.6 entirely (each process has its own RNG
        state). Portability constraints, though:

        -   **`parallel::mclapply()` is not an option.** It is
            fork-based, and R ships a Windows stub whose body is
            `if (cores > 1L) stop("'mc.cores' > 1 is not supported on
            Windows")` -- a hard error, not a fallback. That would
            break the package on Alex's machine and on CRAN's Windows
            check. Even on Linux/macOS, forking a session with a live
            threaded-BLAS or OpenMP pool (OpenBLAS on most Linux
            distros, Accelerate on macOS) is a well-known deadlock
            source -- and doubly so if A.6 is fixed by *keeping*
            OpenMP.
        -   **`parallel::makeCluster()` (PSOCK) + `parLapply()` works
            on all three platforms**, and
            `parallel::clusterSetRNGStream()` gives reproducible,
            independent L'Ecuyer streams per chain, which is strictly
            better than the current situation. The cost is that
            workers are fresh R sessions
            (`clusterEvalQ(cl, library(occJSDM))`, plus serialising
            the data out and the per-chain arrays back) -- negligible
            against a multi-minute MCMC, though the return trip is not
            free given how large `Bs_output`/`U_output` are (see D.9).
        -   **Make it opt-in**: a `cores = 1L` argument, serial by
            default, so existing behaviour is unchanged and CRAN's
            two-core limit for examples/tests/vignettes is respected.

        Structurally this needs the chain body extracted into a
        function returning its own `*_output_chain` arrays -- mechanical,
        since the loop already writes only to per-chain objects. The one
        piece of genuinely shared state is the WAIC accumulator, which
        currently streams across chains sequentially; parallelising
        forces one accumulator per chain plus a merge, which is exactly
        what the fix for bug A.4 requires anyway (`mean_lik` is a plain
        mean; `M2` merges with the standard parallel-variance formula).
        The `z_output_mean` / `psi_output_mean` / `w_output_mean` /
        `theta_output_mean` running means merge by simple addition of
        the per-chain partials.

    2.  **Drop the `options(mc.cores = ...)` call in `.onLoad()`.**
        `R/zzz.R` sets a global option at load time, which changes the
        user's session state and affects every other package that reads
        `mc.cores` -- CRAN policy is explicitly against this. It should
        be replaced by the `cores` argument in D.1. (Also
        `parallel::detectCores()` can return `NA`, which
        `min(2L, NA)` happily propagates.)

    2.  **Stop computing variance partitioning every iteration.**
        `computeVariancePartitioning_stdevs()` is called from inside
        `update_jSDMcoef()` (`R/jsdmfun.R:1083`) on every single
        iteration, including all of burn-in, and each call does seven
        `SD()` evaluations, each of which is
        `apply(logistic(eta), 2, sd)` over an `n x S` matrix. It is only
        ever consumed at stored iterations
        (`R/runOccJSDM.R:1174`). Move it out of `update_jSDMcoef()` and
        compute it in `runOccJSDM()` only when
        `iter > nburn & (iter - nburn) %% nthin == 0`: a 50% reduction
        in these calls at the vignette's settings, 95% at
        `nthin = 10`. While there, replace `apply(X, 2, sd)` with a
        vectorised column-SD.

    3.  **`computePsiCoef()` is called three times per iteration.**
        `R/jsdmfun.R:984`, `:1052` and `:1074`. Each call recomputes
        `t(computeBtcoef(...))`, `X %*% B` (`n x p` by `p x S`),
        `KsBproduct()` and `H %*% L`. The second call exists only to
        refresh `XB`/`SE` before `sample_U_cpp()`, but neither depends
        on `U`, so they are unchanged from the first call; and the
        third differs from the second only in the updated `U`. Call it
        once at the top, reuse `XB`/`SE`, then recompute just
        `UL <- U %*% L` and `eta <- XB + SE + UL` at the end -- roughly
        a two-thirds saving on this block.

    4.  **Hoist loop-invariant work out of the per-species loop in
        `sample_BBsL()`.** `XU <- cbind(1, X, U)`, `B_current` and
        `invB_current` (`R/jsdmfun.R:709-713`) are identical for all
        `S` species but are rebuilt inside the loop, allocating `S`
        copies of an `n x (1 + p + d)` matrix per iteration. Only the
        `sigma_b^2` diagonal depends on anything that varies, and
        `sigma_b` is fixed within a call.

    5.  **Precompute the constant parts of the `c_imk` update.**
        `R/runOccJSDM.R:1104` recomputes `y > 0` (an `N3 x S` logical)
        every iteration although `y` never changes; and
        `w_all <- w[idx_w_k, , drop = FALSE]` (`:1100`) materialises a
        second `N3 x S` copy. Hoist `y_pos <- (y > 0)` above the chain
        loop, and consider folding the `w_all` gather into
        `sample_pq_cpp()` so the copy never reaches R.

    6.  **Make the WAIC accumulation optional, and cheaper.** The three
        `computeModelLoglik*_cpp()` calls evaluate `R::dbinom` over
        `n*S + N*S + N3*S` elements at every stored iteration. For
        binary data `dbinom(y, 1, p, log = TRUE)` is just
        `y*log(p) + (1-y)*log(1-p)`, several times faster than the
        general call, and `log(p)` / `log(1-p)` can be tabulated once
        per iteration (`sample_w_cim_cipp()` already does exactly this
        at `src/functions.cpp:458-469`). Also add a
        `computeWAIC = TRUE/FALSE` argument for users who are not doing
        model comparison.

    7.  **Vectorise the starting-value loops.**
        `R/runOccJSDM.R:946-961` and `:974-981` are triple-nested R
        loops over `S x n x M` to initialise `w` and `z`. Negligible on
        the vignette dataset, slow for realistic `S`. Both reduce to
        grouped "any positive" reductions:
        `w` from `rowsum(y > 0, idx_w_k) > 0`, `z` from
        `rowsum(w, idx_z_w) > 0`.

    8.  **Do not allocate posterior arrays that are never filled.**
        With `summarisedLatentPresences = FALSE`, `w_output`
        (`N x S x niter x nchain`) is allocated and never written, as
        are `w_output_chain` and `theta_output_chain` (see B.1). More
        generally, `Bs_output` (`ps x S x niter x nchain`) and
        `U_output` (`n x d x niter x nchain`) are the two largest
        components of the 62 MB `sampleresults.rda`; a `keep =`
        argument selecting which blocks to retain, or storing the
        latent-factor blocks pre-thinned, would address both the
        runtime allocation and the CRAN size blocker.

    9.  **Reduce the repeated `arma::inv()` calls in the samplers.**
        `sample_beta_cpp()` (`src/functions.cpp:249-253`), `sampleB()`
        and `sampleBuniv()` (`src/jsdm.cpp:579-583`, `:600-604`) each
        call `arma::inv(B)` twice plus
        `arma::inv(arma::trimatl(L))`, executed `S` or `n` times per
        iteration. In every caller `B` is diagonal, so this is a dense
        general inverse of a diagonal matrix. `sampleB_SoR()`
        (`src/jsdm.cpp:817-839`) already shows the right pattern: take
        the precision directly as an argument, and draw via a
        triangular solve against a standard normal instead of forming
        the inverse Cholesky factor explicitly.

**Outreach**

1.  Listserv announcement (beta release), drafted July 20 2026:

    > Subject: New R package (beta) — occJSDM, for eDNA occupancy/JSDM
    > modeling
    >
    > Hi all,
    >
    > Announcing **occJSDM**, an R package for jointly modeling eDNA
    > metabarcoding data across species
    > (<https://github.com/AlexDiana/occJSDM>). Note this is **beta
    > software**, under active development.
    >
    > occJSDM extends the two-stage eDNA occupancy model of Ji et al.
    > (2025, *Ecology Letters*, <doi:10.1111/ele.70302>) — which
    > separates field capture from PCR/lab detection error, per species
    > — by adding a joint species distribution model (JSDM) layer.
    > Highlights:
    >
    > - Models both false negatives and false positives at each
    >   detection stage (field capture and PCR/lab), per species.
    > - Integrates occupancy modeling with a full-featured JSDM: species
    >   fit jointly, with latent-factor residual correlations rather
    >   than one at a time.
    > - Supports species traits shaping occupancy responses, and
    >   optional spatial autocorrelation (GP kernel) across sites.
    > - MCMC fitting with diagnostics, variance partitioning,
    >   ordination, and residual correlation outputs built in.
    >
    > Vignettes included for simulation and model
    > fitting/interpretation. Feedback (and bug reports) very welcome.
    >
    > [Your name]
